Agent-assembled affine-cover criterion with canonical kernel identification.

proof.text: Fix a chart and omit its index. Restrict the given short exact A-module sequence to R; its maps and underlying groups are unchanged, so it remains short exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] over R, with flat last term N and arbitrary tensor factor S. Swap tensor factors by the maps s⊗l↦l⊗s (and their inverses), obtaining exactness of 0→L⊗_R S→M⊗_R S→N⊗_R S→0. The maps commute with the A⊗_R S action since p and q are A-linear. The supplied commuting section isomorphisms therefore give short exactness on Q. This uses neither flatness of S nor flatness of A.

Put B=O_Y(Q). For c∈B, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) makes D(c) affine with ring B_c. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] to D(c)⊆Q and each of F,G,H: its map t⊗b↦b(t|_{D(c)}) identifies P(D(c)) with P(Q)⊗_B B_c, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] identifies P(Q)⊗_B B_c with the localized B-module P(Q)_c, t⊗(b/c^n)↦bt/c^n, carrying a⊗1 to a_c (P=F,G,H). For a sheaf morphism a, a(t|/c^n)=a(t)|/c^n by restriction compatibility and linearity. Thus both arrows are exactly the localizations of the chart tensor arrows under these isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] to the full exact sequence, including the pairs 0→F(Q)→G(Q) and G(Q)→H(Q)→0. Localization of the zero module is zero, so this proves all three exactness assertions on D(c), including c=0 and zero chart rings.

The composite vu vanishes: for a section over any open W and x∈W, choose Q_λ containing x, then a principal D(c) with x∈D(c)⊆W∩Q_λ using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), transported to Q_λ≅Spec O_Y(Q_λ) by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a). Step 2 gives vu=0 on sections over D(c). These D(c) cover W, so the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives zero on W. Let K=ker v, computed sectionwise as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let k:F→K be u with codomain restricted to the kernel. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], K is quasi-coherent, since G and H are. On each Q_λ, k is the map F(Q_λ)→ker(v_{Q_λ}) induced by u_{Q_λ}; step 1 says it is injective and surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover] to k on the given affine covering. Hence k is an isomorphism, and its composite with K→G is u by construction.

proof.text: By step 1, v is surjective on sections of every Q_λ; H is quasi-coherent. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-quasicoherent-epi-affine-cover] makes v an epimorphism. The isomorphism k in step 3 identifies u with the kernel inclusion, so u is monic and its image is ker v. Together with vu=0 these are exactly the short exactness conditions of [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The factorization k is canonical because the kernel inclusion is monic. All arguments use individual members of the cover, with no finiteness assumptions on it or the modules.

title: Relative-flat tensor chart criterion for sheaf short exactness
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal H$ be morphisms of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $Y$ has an affine open covering $(Q_\lambda)_{\lambda\in L}$ with the following data for each $\lambda$: commutative rings $R_\lambda,A_\lambda,S_\lambda$, homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to A_\lambda$ and $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, an isomorphism $\mathcal O_Y(Q_\lambda)\cong A_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}S_\lambda$, and a short exact sequence of $A_\lambda$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow L_\lambda\xrightarrow{p_\lambda}M_\lambda\xrightarrow{q_\lambda}N_\lambda\longrightarrow0$$
[def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Assume $N_\lambda$ is flat as an $R_\lambda$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Supply $A_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}S_\lambda$-linear isomorphisms from the section sequence $(\mathcal F(Q_\lambda),u_{Q_\lambda},\mathcal G(Q_\lambda),v_{Q_\lambda},\mathcal H(Q_\lambda))$ to
$$L_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}S_\lambda\xrightarrow{p_\lambda\otimes1}M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}S_\lambda\xrightarrow{q_\lambda\otimes1}N_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}S_\lambda,$$
meaning that both squares commute. Then this section sequence is short exact on every $Q_\lambda$ and every principal open $D(c)\subseteq Q_\lambda$, $c\in\mathcal O_Y(Q_\lambda)$: on $D(c)$ its maps are precisely the localizations at $\{1,c,c^2,\ldots\}$ of the displayed tensor maps. The sheaf sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal F\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal H\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact, and the canonical factorization $\mathcal F\to\ker v$ is an isomorphism whose composite with the kernel inclusion is $u$. No flatness of $A_\lambda$ or $S_\lambda$ over $R_\lambda$ and no finiteness of the cover or the modules is required.
